clue.text: What those who travel abroad can get for money

definitions.text: What those who travel abroad can get for money

parts.words: What those who travel abroad can get for money
parts.note: reads like a question about souvenirs or bargains, but describes the figure that sets how much foreign currency your pounds will buy

explanation.surface: A traveller wonders what their cash will fetch abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure banks quote tells a tourist how many units of foreign currency each pound buys, which is exactly what they get for their money.

clue.text: Polychromatic arch as a change from a brown one

indicators.note: a change from these letters means they are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A colourful arch is set against a plain brown one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as a change from' looks like a comparison, but 'change' is the anagram signal: A BROWN plus I (one) is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The arc of seven colours seen in the sky after rain is the classic many-coloured arch.

clue.text: Last thing a patriotic French audience will stand for

definitions.text: Last thing a patriotic French audience will stand for

parts.words: Last thing a patriotic French audience will stand for
parts.note: 'the last thing they will stand for' usually means something they would never tolerate, but here it is what they literally rise to their feet for at the end of an event

explanation.surface: Patriotic French people supposedly refuse to tolerate something.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'the last thing I'd stand for' means something intolerable; read literally it is the anthem played at the end, for which the French audience stands.
explanation.definitionFit: France's national anthem is played at the close of events and audiences rise for it.

clue.text: Great distinction conferred on an Arab sultanate

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on top of another comes first

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a high British honour

explanation.surface: A great honour is bestowed on someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit (OM) is one of Britain's most exclusive honours; it sits above AN.
explanation.definitionFit: This Gulf state on the Arabian Peninsula is ruled by a sultan.

clue.text: The opposite of a West country domain?

parts.note: the compass point opposite west is east, abbreviated E
a state is a country or nation

explanation.surface: Someone asks what lies at the opposite end of the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West country' looks like the region of south-west England (Cornwall, Devon and so on), but it splits: the opposite of West gives E, and country gives STATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A landed property or holding of land is someone's domain.

clue.text: Free-wheeling kind of agnos tic

indicators.note: a kind of the word means a version of it with the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A relaxed sort of religious doubter.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'agnes tic', a misread of 'agnostic'; 'kind of' signals an anagram of AGNOSTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving along without pedalling or engine power is freewheeling.

clue.text: Untruth swallowed by a nation that brings about estrangement

indicators.note: one thing swallowed by another goes inside it

parts.note: taken as written
an untruth is a lie

explanation.surface: A country swallows a falsehood and becomes estranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Alienation is the state of being isolated or cut off from others, a synonym of estrangement.

clue.text: A good deal of magnanimous legislation?

parts.note: magnanimous means generous
a measure is a piece of legislation, a bill or act

explanation.surface: A large amount of big-hearted law-making.
explanation.definitionFit: A generous measure is an ample portion, a large quantity.

clue.text: The coming of the Christian faith

definitions.text: The coming of the Christian faith

parts.words: The coming of the Christian faith
parts.note: reads as the arrival of Christianity somewhere, but describes the church season awaiting Christ's coming, a word that also just means arrival

explanation.surface: Christianity arrives in a land.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means arrival, and in the church calendar names the season before Christmas awaiting Christ's coming.

clue.text: Nice tax adjustment that isn't quite true

indicators.note: an adjustment of these letters rearranges them into a new order

explanation.surface: A French city adjusts a tax, and the figures are off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like the adjective but is the French city; its letters with TAX are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not precisely accurate is imprecise, falling short of quite correct.

clue.text: Properly dressed for parade

parts.note: suggests wearing correct uniform, but in drill 'dress' means to line up straight

explanation.surface: A soldier is turned out smartly for the parade ground.
explanation.walkthrough: In military drill, to 'dress' ranks is to bring them into a straight line.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops that have dressed their ranks stand in a straight, even line.

clue.text: Il Fibre found 'in ruined barn

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Roughage is found in a derelict farm building.
explanation.definitionFit: The husks of cereal grain are a source of dietary roughage.

clue.text: A Government tender, possibly

parts.note: a tender sounds like a bid for a government contract, but here it is someone who tends patients and is registered by the state

explanation.surface: A firm bids for a public contract.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurse is one who tends the sick, and one qualified on the official register is state-recognised.

clue.text: Hot soup taken in by medical orderly

indicators.note: one thing taken in by another goes inside it
in soup means in a mess, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A hospital orderly brings in hot soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soup' scrambles HOT into THO, and 'taken in by' puts it inside MEDICAL, between ME and DICAL; 'orderly' looks like the hospital porter but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Methodical means systematic and well organised.

clue.text: When' war is about she may tighten things up

indicators.note: about means around or in disarray, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: In wartime a woman takes on the job of tightening things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'she' looks like the subject of the sentence, but its letters join WAR in the anagram signalled by 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: This little ring is fitted under a nut or bolt head so it holds tight.

clue.text: Isn't curt when ordered to teach

indicators.note: letters ordered are put into a fresh sequence

explanation.surface: Someone is not brusque when told to give lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ISN'T and CURT are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To instruct someone is to educate or train them.

clue.text: She is in the 'grip of devious rascal.

indicators.note: something in the grip of another is held inside it
devious means winding or crooked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman is held fast by a scheming scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devious' scrambles RASCAL into CLARSA; 'in the grip of' puts IS inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, so it stands for a female person.

clue.text: Not very' cunning about what comes with the dawn

indicators.note: one word placed about another surrounds it

parts.note: cunning means sly
daybreak brings light

explanation.surface: A sly person is not very clever around daybreak.
explanation.definitionFit: Slightly means to a small degree, not very much.

clue.text: Bands of salvation Army girls?

parts.note: girls are shes, female persons

explanation.surface: The bands of Salvation Army women.
explanation.walkthrough: The Salvation Army is famous for its brass bands, so 'Bands' looks part of the scene; it is the definition, meaning strips of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribbons or strips of cloth worn around the waist or over the shoulder are bands.

clue.text: The Upper First on the Gulf of Gaeta?

parts.note: the first form is the first-year class in a British school, written as form I
a class streamed by ability puts the higher group in section A

explanation.surface: A school class is placed in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: British schools named classes by year and stream, so the upper first-year class was Form IA.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal town in Lazio, Italy, it sits on that gulf between Rome and Naples.

clue.text: If nothing else, can be made to eat last

indicators.note: these letters can be made into something new by rearranging them

explanation.surface: A fussy diner can be made to eat last.
explanation.definitionFit: As a minimum, at any rate: the phrase means if nothing more.

clue.text: Huge fish the petty officer caught in a mountain lake

indicators.note: something caught in another is held inside it

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake
PO is the abbreviation for petty officer

explanation.surface: A naval officer lands a giant fish in a mountain lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A large game fish of warm Atlantic waters, it can exceed two metres.

clue.text: Shrill outcry about a youth dressing for dinner, maybe

indicators.note: one word placed about others surrounds them

parts.note: a scream is a shrill cry
a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: A youngster shrieks while dressing for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressing for dinner' suggests changing clothes; it is a sauce for salad.
explanation.definitionFit: A creamy bottled sauce poured on salads is a dressing.

clue.text: Retrospective enactment I inwardly lament

indicators.note: placed inwardly means put inside
looking back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an enactment is a law

explanation.surface: Someone privately regrets a backdated piece of legislation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retrospective' turns LAW into WAL; 'inwardly' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To wail is to cry out in grief, a synonym of lament.

clue.text: No matter to object to?

definitions.meaning: the intellect as opposed to physical substance

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether it matters enough to protest.
explanation.definitionFit: The thinking self is contrasted with physical substance, and the verb means to take offence at.

clue.text: Venice's variety shows

indicators.note: a variety of the letters is a different arrangement of them

explanation.surface: Venetian variety theatre performances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety shows' looks like a theatre phrase; 'variety' signals the anagram and 'shows' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Evinces means displays or reveals.

clue.text: Paul excitedly grasping a border flower

indicators.note: one piece grasping another holds it inside
behaving excitedly means jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: An excited gardener named Paul clutches a plant from the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'border' looks like a flower bed; it gives RIM, which goes inside ULA, the rearranged PAUL.
explanation.definitionFit: The primrose and polyanthus belong to this genus of spring-flowering plants.

clue.text: Time off from work that shouldn't be begrudged

definitions.text: Time off from work that shouldn't be begrudged

parts.words: Time off from work that shouldn't be begrudged
parts.note: a straightforward description of a break someone has truly deserved through hard effort

explanation.surface: Someone deserves a holiday after hard toil.
explanation.definitionFit: A break fully merited by effort is one nobody could resent.
